parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> TFN is a travel business which sells holidays. It has 37 shops and 1000 employees. Last year TFN’s profit increased to \$46 million. The Managing Director knows that good communication is essential to maintain customer loyalty.

**Outline two** barriers to communication that TFN may experience.
parts.solution_md:
Employees may use jargon **[K] **that the customers do not understand when booking holidays **[Ap]**

There may be noise and distractions **[K] **in the call centre with 1000 employees that make it difficult to hear customer holiday concerns** [Ap]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Outline questions always require you to make use of the case study information to support your points

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2; Application 2
> 
>   - Give two valid benefits to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - For each benefit, refer to the business case study to achieve both application [Ap] marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Barriers may include:
> 
>   - Use of jargon [K] that may confuse customers when discussing holiday bookings [Ap]
>   - Noise and distractions in a busy call centre [K] that make it hard for employees to understand customer concerns [Ap]
>   - Language differences [K] between employees and international customers [Ap]
>   - Poor internet connection or technical faults [K] affecting online bookings or emails [Ap]
> - Other appropriate responses should also be credited

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Gloria is a sole trader. Her business provides house-cleaning services. Gloria uses telephone calls to communicate with her 4 employees and her customers. Sometimes she forgets to call customers back and risks damaging her business reputation. There have been incorrect invoices sent to customers in the past.

**Outline two** forms of written communication Gloria could introduce to improve record keeping in her business.
parts.solution_md:
Gloria could record each telephone call with a customer on a special form **[K]** that will give her a record of cleaning requirements **[Ap]**

Employees could write down the hours worked cleaning **[Ap]** for a customer that can be checked against an invoice **[K] **before sending to avoid mistakes

> **[exam-tip]**
> Outline questions always require you to make use of the case study information to support your points

**Alternative ways to answer**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2; Application 2
> 
>   - Give two valid benefits to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - For each benefit, refer to the business case study to achieve both application [Ap] marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Forms may include:
> 
>   - Using a customer contact log or special form to record phone calls [K] so she remembers customer cleaning needs [Ap]
>   - Introducing timesheets for employees [K] to track hours spent on each cleaning job for invoice accuracy [Ap]
>   - Using a job sheet or checklist [K] to note what tasks have been completed for each customer [Ap]
>   - Creating a customer feedback form [K] that helps improve service and track satisfaction [Ap]
> - Other appropriate responses should also be credited

One-way communication is a message to a stakeholder** [K]*** *that does not require a response **[K]**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**Sports Safety Equipment (SSE)**

SSE manufactures sports safety equipment in country Z. It is a public limited company which has been successful for over 30 years. The main product SSE manufactures is safety helmets for different sports, such as bicycle riding, cricket and skateboarding. SSE has one large factory making the safety helmets. The factory uses flow production. The production workers each specialise in one task on the production line. SSE’s raw materials are imported.

SSE sells its helmets in several other countries and is planning to expand into many more. It will need to carry out market research before entering new markets in other countries. Each country has different sports that are popular and the style of helmets varies from country to country.

SSE plans to build its own factories in its most important markets in other countries and will need to choose a suitable source of finance. The Human Resources Director has decided to use internal recruitment for the managers of the new factories. There will need to be effective communication between the managers of the new factories and SSE’s head office in country Z.

Most of SSE’s sales in country Z are through sports equipment shops. Customers like to try on the helmets to check they fit correctly. SSE currently sells its helmets in other countries through its website.

SSE is also increasing its product range. The latest new product being developed is a children’s cricket helmet. A break-even chart for this new product is shown in Appendix 3.

**Appendix 1 **

**Extract from SSE’s website **

**If you want the best protection when playing sport then buy an SSE safety helmet!**

We supply a wide range of safety helmets for you when playing sport.

Whatever the sport - SSE produces a helmet for you.

You can order directly from this website by entering your head measurements below.

Get the perfect fit for you!

**Appendix 2 **

**Email from SSE’s Managing Director to SSE’s Finance Director**

To: Finance Director

From: Managing Director

Date: 1 September 2023

Re: Demand for SSE’s products Demand for SSE’s products in country Z is forecast to increase. Our government has imposed import tariffs on safety helmets. We may be able to increase our prices.

The exchange rate in country Z is expected to fall. However, other countries have introduced import quotas on safety helmets.

We will have to consider all the likely effects of these changes.

**Appendix 3 **

**Projected weekly break-even chart for SSE’s new children’s cricket helmet**

The maximum output and sales for this product is 1000 units per week.

Consider how the following **three **barriers could make communication less effective between SSE’s head office in country Z and its new factories in other countries.

- Problem with the medium used
- Problem with the sender
- Problem with the receiver

Which barrier would be the easiest to overcome? **Justify **your choice.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2023-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
A problem with the medium used could arise if SSE relies too heavily on email for urgent messages. For example, if the head office needs to quickly inform a new factory about a change in helmet design specifications **[Ap]**, an email could get lost in a spam folder or not be seen immediately. This could lead to production delays or mistakes **[An]**

The sender of messages from SSE's head office may create barriers by using technical jargon about helmet manufacturing **[Ap] **that managers in the new factories don't understand. Or they might send overly long messages with too much information, causing important points about safety standards to be overlooked and helmets failing to meet them, causing wastage **[An]**

Receivers in the new factories could cause communication problems if they don't carefully read messages from head office. They may also misinterpret instructions about helmet production targets **[Ap]** if they speak a different language and don't fully grasp the nuances, giving SSE less output to sell **[An]**

The easiest barrier to overcome is likely the problem with the sender **[E]**. SSE could provide training to head office staff in country Z **[Ap]** on writing clear, concise messages without jargon. They could also create templates for common communications such as emails or staff notices to ensure important information is highlighted. Addressing these sender issues would improve communication regardless of the medium used or receiver's situation **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Problems with the medium used**
> 
>   - Too many links in the chain → each person may change the wording → final message is distorted
>   - Message can be lost → receiver never reads it → task (e.g. making helmets) is not done
>   - Wrong channel for the situation → slow delivery when speed is vital (letter vs phone)
>   - Technical breakdown → no internet / dead battery → message never reaches receiver
> - **Problems with the sender**
> 
>   - Unclear wording → jargon or speaking too fast → receiver misunderstands
>   - Message is overloaded → key facts about, say, cricket helmets are hidden → action not taken
>   - Sent to the wrong person or wrong file → message ignored → decision delayed
> - **Problems with the receiver**
> 
>   - Not listening → misses phone instructions about component orders
>   - Does not trust the sender → hesitates to act on the information
>   - Poor attitude / low urgency → delays action
>   - Language barrier → misunderstands key points
> 
> **Conclusion**
> 
> - **Medium issues** are often the easiest to fix: ask for quick feedback; if none arrives, resend the message
> - **Sender issues** can be reduced with clear, short language guidelines for everyone
> - **Receiver issues** may need culture-building (e.g. flagging urgent messages) but can still be overcome with clear priority labels

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**Furniture Outdoors (FO)**

FO has been a private limited company for 20 years. It is owned and run by the Chan family and is located in country Z. In country Z the secondary sector has become relatively more important as the country has developed. FO is a manufacturer of wooden furniture that is suitable for outdoor use. Its products include tables, chairs and other outdoor furniture.

Customers order online from the FO website. The furniture is then delivered to customers in country Z using FO’s own delivery vehicles. However, FO is considering changing to selling its furniture through either wholesalers or large retailers in country Z.

The Chan family have the business objective of contributing to sustainable development. FO only uses sustainably sourced wood when making furniture. This is from local forests in country Z and the wood is more expensive than imported alternatives.

For many years FO shareholders have reinvested profits to provide the finance for growth. FO recently took over 2 other furniture businesses in country Z and plans further takeovers. The Chan family plan to continue to control and manage FO after this expansion. The leadership style of these two companies is very different to that of FO and their factories are located several miles away from FO in different regions of country Z.

FO need to manage all its resources effectively. It tries to use the same components such as nails, brackets and paint for all its furniture designs. It is important to not run out of raw materials and so orders to suppliers must be carefully planned to avoid late deliveries. FO want to keep wastage of materials to a minimum. FO also need to consider how many employees are required to complete each order.

**Appendix 1 - FO website advertisement**

**FO - the only business to go to when you need new outdoor furniture for your garden. **

FO produce a range of high quality furniture to meet all your needs for fashionable, well designed outdoor furniture. Be reassured our furniture is only made from the highest quality wood from sustainable forests.

Our furniture is only available online so order today and have your furniture delivered in the next few weeks. Email any questions to us and we will reply quickly.

**Appendix 2**

**Extract of cost, selling price and sales data for one of FO’s products**

| **Fixed cost per month** | \$10 000 |
|---|---|
| **Variable cost per table** | \$125 |
| **Selling price per table** | \$250 |
| **Forecasts sales for tables per month** | 100 |

**Appendix 3 **

**Newspaper article from the Daily News April 2021 **

**Sustainable production needed to save the planet **

A report from the International Committee for the Planet states that manufacturers must find more sustainable ways to produce their products as global warming is becoming more of an issue.

The report suggests three main ways manufacturers can change:

- Only use raw materials from sources that replace what they have used. This is estimated to raise variable costs by 20%
- Only use packaging that can be recycled. Costs are estimated to increase but the selling price may not rise by more than 10%
- Only use electric vehicles to deliver products. The cost of buying electric vehicles is more than petrol or diesel vehicles. Using electric vehicles could enable variable costs to be reduced by 5%.

Consider the benefits and limitations of the following **three **methods of communication FO could use.

- Email
- Mobile (cell) phone
- Letter

Which method of communication would be most suitable when contacting suppliers about a late delivery? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/0450-june-2021-insert-paper-2-cie-igcse-business---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Email is quick and can reach multiple suppliers at once. FO could easily send details about missing wood, nails or paint **[Ap] **to several suppliers. However, emails may go unread or end up in junk folders, potentially delaying responses about late materials **[An]**

Mobile phones allow for immediate two-way communication. FO could call suppliers to urgently discuss late deliveries of brackets or other components needed for manufacturing outdoor furniture **[Ap]**. However, it may be time-consuming to reach the right person, especially if FO needs to contact multiple suppliers about various raw materials **[An]**

Letters provide a formal record, which could be useful if there are ongoing issues with late deliveries affecting FO's production schedule and it needs to seek compensation **[An]**. However, letters are slow, which is problematic when FO needs materials quickly to fulfil its online **[Ap]** customer orders **[An]**

Email would likely be most suitable for contacting suppliers about late deliveries **[E]**. It balances speed and detail, so FO can quickly send specific information about missing materials to multiple suppliers. This is crucial, as FO needs to manage its resources carefully to avoid production delays and ensure online customers **[Ap]** receive orders promptly **[E]**. While a phone call might be faster for a single supplier, email is more efficient for contacting several suppliers about various late materials. Email also provides a written record FO can reference, unlike phone calls **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Email**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Sent in seconds → suppliers get the message fast, even in another country.
>     - One click reaches many suppliers at once → saves time compared with phoning each one.
>     - Can be printed or saved → FO keeps a hard-copy record for later checks.
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - No guarantee the supplier opens it **→** message may sit in a junk folder.
>     - Needs a good internet link **→** delays if the network is down.
>     - High inbox traffic **→** email could be lost among other messages.
> - **Mobile (cell) phone**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Call is heard instantly **→** FO knows the message reached the right person.
>     - Two-way conversation **→** supplier can answer questions about brackets or delivery times.
>     - Most people keep phones with them **→** easier to reach busy suppliers.
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - May ring several numbers before finding the right contact **→** time-consuming.
>     - International calls and time-zone differences **→** can be costly or inconvenient.
>     - No written record **→** details could be forgotten or disputed later.
> - **Letter**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Provides a formal, signed hard copy **→** useful for legal or large orders.
>     - Plenty of space to explain problems, e.g. late nails and paint.
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Slowest method **→** may add days to order resolution.
>     - Printing and postage costs higher than email or quick calls.
>     - Still no certainty the letter is received unless sent “signed-for”.
> 
> **Conclusion**
> 
> - **Email**: best when many suppliers must be updated quickly and FO needs a written record.
> - **Mobile phone**: gives instant feedback for urgent questions but is slower for multiple suppliers and leaves no paper trail.
> - **Letter: **suits detailed or formal issues yet is too slow for day-to-day delays.
> - FO should match the method to the situation: urgent delivery queries → email or phone; formal contract changes → letter.

parts.problem_md: Do you think having regular meetings is a better way for a business to communicate with part-time employees than using text messages? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Meetings allow two-way communication and immediate feedback **[K]**. This allows ideas to be discussed so instructions or information can be checked for understanding straight away **[An]**

If text messages are sent, employees have a hard copy or record **[K]** of the message to refer back to later if they need to check details **[An]**

As part-time members of staff work different hours, it may be difficult to find a time when all workers are present for a meeting **[E]**.  It may be more convenient for part-time workers to check and read texts during their working hours if it is available on their phone **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include
> 
>   - Meetings:
>   
>     - Allow two-way communication/immediate feedback/allows ideas to be discussed [k] so can explain if instructions/information is not understood (straightaway) [an]
>     - Information can be given out quickly/more detailed [k]
>     - Message can be reinforced by being able to see the speaker/body language of attendees [k]
>     - May take time/be difficult to arrange [k] as part-time employees do not work all the time [an]
>     - Will take people away from work [k] leading to lower output/ lower efficiency/missed sales [an]
>   - Text messages:
>   
>     - No guarantee read/may not have a phone [k] leading to mistakes/wasting resources [an]
>     - Have a hard copy/record [k] which can be referred to later [an]
>     - Can send at any time [k] allowing people to read it when it is convenient for them to do so [an]
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
>   - Advantages of one method can be presented as disadvantages of the other method but do not award the same point twice as mirror answers are not accepted
>   - For evaluation to be awarded justification will usually follow on from relevant analysis of points
>   - To access the evaluation marks candidates must refer to part-time workers

parts.problem_md: **Explain four **reasons why effective communication between the owner and employees in a business is important.
parts.solution_md:
Effective communication can help avoid employees making mistakes** [K], **especially if they lack experience and only know how to carry out a few tasks and need to be told what to do** [An]**

It can improve motivation** [K]**, as communicating regularly and positively with members of staff could encourage them to work harder** [An]**

It can ensure customers are given accurate information by staff **[K]**,** **which may reduce complaints **[An]**

It can encourage feedback from staff** [K]**, which can improve the efficiency of operation of the business** [An]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - In your answer:
> 
>   - Give four valid reasons related to the question → 4 K marks
>   - For each reason, explain how or why it matters using a cause–effect link → 4 An marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Relevant reasons might include:
> 
>   - to ensure instructions are understood
>   - to ensure employees carry out the instructions correctly
>   - to ensure mistakes are not made
>   - to ensure the business works efficiently
>   - to ensure customers are given correct information
>   - to find customer preferences from employees
>   - inaccuracy causes poor reputation
>   - collaboration is better between worker and owner
>   - motivation is better between worker and owner

parts.problem_md: **Explain two **possible methods of internal communication that a small business could use to inform workers about a possible expansion. **Justify **which method should be chosen.
parts.solution_md:
A meeting **[K]** could be held to inform workers, providing the opportunity to ask questions or raise concerns about the expansion. However, this will take staff away from their work so output  could fall **[An]**

An email **[K]** to all workers at the same time allows staff to read it at their own convenience and refer back to it if necessary. However, not all workers might have internet access to read the email **[An]**

A meeting might be best because it allows two-way communication** [E]**. Care must be taken to ensure that workers on different shifts can attend, though, or they may hear information about the expansion second-hand, which could cause conflict **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Relevant points might include:
> 
>   - Meeting (1)
>   
>     - So able to see reactions to ideas/comments. (1)
>     - Will increase costs for travel. (1)
>     - Will take people away from work. (1)
>   - Email (1)/Internal social media (1)
>   
>     - Allows people to read information in own time/have copy for future reference. (1)
>     - Must have access to internet so may have to pay cost of computer for staff. (1)
>   - Justification might include:
>   
>     - Emails because meeting difficult to arrange if people are based in different places so not everyone might be able to attend. (2)
>     - Meetings because in a small business people might not have access to internet so are not able to respond. (2)
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited

parts.problem_md: **Explain four **barriers to communication for a business.
parts.solution_md:
The message could be too long **[K]**,  so the main meaning of the message may be lost in the detail **[An]**

There may be an internet outage **[K]**, which means an email or WhatsApp message may not be received **[An]**

No acknowledgement of receipt is given** [K]** so the sender may be unaware the message was not received **[An]**

The message may contain too much jargon **[K]** so the receiver does not understand the meaning of the information** [An]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - In your answer:
> 
>   - Give four valid reasons related to the question → 4 K marks
>   - For each reason, explain how or why it matters using a cause–effect link → 4 An marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Reasons could include:
> 
>   - Problems with the sender – the language used is not clear/use of jargon or technical terms so do not understand instructions
>   - The message is too long/too much detail is included in the message – so the main meaning of the message may be lost in the detail
>   - Problems with the medium/method – the wrong medium is used such as putting an urgent message on a noticeboard so may not be seen immediately
>   - Computer failure/internet connection/technology fails – the message may not be received
>   - No feedback is given – so the sender is unaware the message has not been received
>   - Problems with the receiver – if a meeting is used and it goes on a long time then the receiver may stop listening
>   - The channel/chain of command may be too long – too many people through which the message is sent it may be distorted
>   - Language differences – hinder understanding of the message

parts.problem_md: **Explain** **two **methods of internal communication a large business could use to share important information with its employees. **Justify **which method should be used.
parts.solution_md:
A video conference meeting could be held **[K] **with all workers to receive the message at the same time. However, during the video conference, staff will not be working so output could fall** [An]**

An email message** [K]** can be sent to all staff so it is received by everyone at the same time. However, all staff may not be online or be able to access the email at the time it is sent** [An]**

An email would be the most convenient and cheapest way to send the information to all its employees at the same time** [E]**. Employees will be able to keep the email to refer back to at a later point if they need to check details of the announcement **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Meeting / briefing / video conference [k] workers receive the message at the same time [an] but workers will not be working so output may fall [an]
>   - Email [k] message can be sent to multiple people at the same time [an] but people may not be able to access the internet [an]
>   - Phones [k] allows for immediate feedback [an]
>   - Text / SMS [k] contains only very limited information [an]
>   - Posters / noticeboards [k]
>   - Announcements [k]
>   - Internal newspapers [k]
>   - Social media such as Whatsapp [k]
>   - Letter [k]
> - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Email [k] would allow the business to send the same message to multiple people [an]. A meeting [k] will allow employees to ask questions to confirm their understanding of the important information [an]. Email is better as it may not be possible to get all employees in a large business together at the same time [eval]. Whereas with an email all employees receive information which they can refer back to later. [eval]
>   - For evaluation to be awarded justification will usually follow on from relevant analysis of points
> - Do not award types of communication such as written, verbal, electronic

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> MBH is a business organisation in the public sector. It controls 5 hospitals and has 5600 employees including 440 doctors. External recruitment is used when recruiting skilled employees. The Human Resources Director uses ideas from Herzberg’s theory to improve employee motivation. He is worried about communication barriers within MBH. The business has a tall organisational structure and a long chain of command. Most of MBH’s internal communication is by email and phone calls.

**Explain **how MBH might reduce or remove each of the following communication barriers:

- Messages lost
- Use of jargon
parts.solution_md:
MBH could require senior managers ask for feedback** [K]**. This would ensure that the message is received and understood by staff [**An**] in the five hospitals [**Ap**]

Staff could be encouraged to use simple language and avoid jargon [**K**] in phone or email communications between internal staff in hospitals **[Ap]** so it is easy for the receiver to understand **[An]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Your answer must focus on the specific barriers to communication listed in the question, not communication barriers in general

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Write two developed paragraphs, one for each part of the question
> - For each paragraph:
> 
>   - State a valid point relevant to the question → 1 K mark
>   - Apply it clearly to the business in the case study → 1 Ap mark
>   - Explain the impact using a cause–effect chain → 1 An mark
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Messages lost:
